rights_topics.title: Domestic Violence & Your Rights
rights_topics.summary: The Domestic Violence Act protects you from physical, sexual, economic and emotional abuse by a spouse, partner or family member. You can apply for a protection order from a Magistrate's Court without needing a lawyer. Police must record your complaint - they cannot turn you away as a family matter.

action_steps.title: If in immediate danger, move somewhere safer
action_steps.description: If you can safely do so, move to a safer location before anything else.

action_steps.title: Call a free helpline
action_steps.description: Sauti 116 or the Police GBV line are both free and available 24/7.

action_steps.title: Ask for a PF3 medical form if injured
action_steps.description: This form is free from a government health centre and helps document your case.

action_steps.title: Apply for a protection order
action_steps.description: You can apply at a Magistrate's Court without needing a lawyer.

safety_responses.message: Your safety matters. You are not alone, and this is not your fault. If you are in immediate danger, consider moving somewhere safer if you can. Free, trusted support: Sauti 116, or the Police GBV line on 0800199195.

rights_topics.title: Property Rights After Separation
rights_topics.summary: Under the Succession Act, a wife - including in a customary marriage - generally has a right to a share of matrimonial property acquired during the marriage, even if it is registered in the husband's name alone.

action_steps.title: Do not sign away property rights
action_steps.description: Avoid signing any documents about the property before getting advice.

action_steps.title: Contact a legal aid clinic
action_steps.description: FIDA Uganda offers free guidance on matrimonial property matters.

action_steps.title: Keep property documents safe
action_steps.description: Hold on to any paperwork related to the property in a safe place.
